title: Is Your Life Congruent with What You Say?
header_line: My analysis of one book on an entrepreneur's life. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Does the way someone lives match what they say they stand for?

groups.heading: What is he repeatedly doing that's not working?

lines.text: I said the chapter ends with the author having trouble in his marriage. I asked: what can we learn from what he is doing in relationships? What is he repeatedly doing that is not working?

A student said: when things start going bad, he doesn't fight for it. He's really good at moving on, but almost a little too good. And he doesn't want to grow with people. He's so hyper focused on business growth, he is not thinking about a partnership of two people.
I agreed: he stays in a bit of a selfish mode. I'm building this business, I've got all these things to do.

Another student said: the fact that he won't look at himself. As an entrepreneur I've had to do this myself. You have to look in the mirror and realize it is not the obstacles out there. It's you against you. He never thought he was the problem.

You have to look at somebody's personal life, I said, to make sure it is in sync with their professional life. The word is congruent. Not self-reflecting is part of his Achilles heel. He accomplishes all these things, but he doesn't self-reflect.

So the takeaway for entrepreneurs, I said: study somebody's personal life and see if they are congruent with the values they talk about in their business life. Are they practicing what they preach? And he is always talking about what he is going to do in the future, so study what he did in the past and what he does day to day in the present.

I read the author's account that he was sent to boarding school at four and learned to cope by himself. I said: he does not rely on people. He is the leader. He is the one who does everything. I can do this by myself.
What would a study of your own personal life say about your business values?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write one thing you repeatedly do that is not working.
Write whether you are the problem, honestly.
Write one value you talk about in business.
Write whether your personal life is congruent with it.
Write one change you will make, personal or professional.

check.q: What word did I use for a personal life that matches business values?
What did a student say the author never thought?
What did I say entrepreneurs should study in a person?
choices: Whether their personal life is congruent with their stated values

recap: Study whether a person's life is congruent with what they say, including your own.
